Negasunt Powder is authorized for this use only for the duration of the declaration that circumstances exist justifying the authorization of the emergency use of Negasunt Powder under section 564(b)(1) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FD&C Act), 21 U.S.C. § 360bbb-3(b)(1), unless the declaration is terminated or the authorization is revoked sooner. Federal law prohibits the extra-label use of this drug. Additional Important Safety Information Not for use in humans. Keep out of reach of children. Only handlers wearing required PPE may be in the area during application. Do not apply in a confined, non-ventilated area; provide thorough ventilation. Call a poison control center or doctor immediately for treatment advice if Negusant Powder is swallowed, inhaled, on skin or clothing, or in eyes. Sulfonamides are contraindicated in animals that are hypersensitive to them and in animals with severe renal or hepatic impairment. For external use only on animals. Do not contaminate water, feed, troughs, feed handling equipment, or milk or meat handling equipment. Use with caution in very young, weak, or debilitated animals. In the case of overdose, treat with atropine sulfate or pralidoxine chloride (2-PAM) as soon as possible. The most common adverse reactions associated with organophosphate and carbamate toxicity in animals include frequent urination and defecation, muscle twitching, and watering eyes. body_text:  LnRiLWhlYWRpbmcuaGFzLWJhY2tncm91bmR7cGFkZGluZzowfQ== TWVycml3ZWF0aGVyOnJlZ3VsYXI=  Blog August 7, 2026 The Hotels AP Automation Benchmark Report: Summer 2026 Edition by Mike Waldron Why This Report Exists Hotel finance runs on property-level accounting, where every invoice has to land in the right department, Rooms, F&B, Spa, and the right entity, before it ever reaches a consolidated GL. For a Controller managing AP across a multi-property portfolio, or a Regional Controller with visibility into a dozen properties at once, a misrouted invoice isn’t just an annoyance. It’s a department that’s miscoded its month, an aging report that doesn’t tell the truth, and a GM asking questions the Controller can’t yet answer. Most operators know there’s leakage somewhere in their AP process. What they don’t have is the data to prove it: exactly how many duplicate invoices are slipping through, exactly how much exposure is sitting in flagged invoices, exactly how much faster the team could be closing if statement reconciliation wasn’t eating an hour per vendor per month. That gap between knowing something’s off and being able to point to it is where hotel AP has always struggled. We process hundreds of thousands of invoices every quarter across our hotel customer base. This report is what that data actually shows, not industry estimates, not survey responses, but numbers pulled from real hotel operations. This is the first edition. Twice a year, we’ll track how these numbers move, flag what’s driving the changes, and give hotel finance teams a benchmark they can actually use. This edition covers duplicate detection, fraud exposure, discrepancy rates, payment errors, invoice lifecycle time, and AP labor savings. Profitability Benchmarks Duplicate Detection Benchmark : Hotel customers saved $471 million on 455,850 duplicate invoices flagged and prevented. In the first half of 2026, hotel accounts caught 265,842 duplicates, preventing $293 million in overspending. Duplicate values have risen every quarter, suggesting either that invoice values are climbing or that vendors are submitting higher-value duplicates. Either way, the trend makes automated detection increasingly critical, not optional, for multi-property operators processing this kind of volume. Invoice Risk Benchmark : 89 percent of hotel customers had at least one invoice flagged for overcharges or fraud. In the first half of 2026, 63 percent of hotel accounts had a flagged invoice, with the flagged invoices averaging $4,817 each. Automated controls are dramatically outperforming manual processes at catching and preventing fraud before it escalates. For a Controller who used to find out about an overcharge during statement reconciliation, weeks after the fact, this is the difference between catching a problem and discovering one. Credit Recovery Benchmark: Ottimate uncovered $488.1 million in credits related to refunds, adjustments, and overcharge corrections last year. In the first half of 2026, Ottimate uncovered $358 million in credits related to refunds, adjustments and overcharges for hotels alone. With continuous pricing increases, and invoice volumes on the rise, we continue to see the amount of overcharges increase. Implementing automation into your workflow is more important than ever to make sure you are catching these costly mistakes before they hit your bottom line. Payments Benchmark : Ottimate caught 14,250 payments with errors last year, accounting for $1.6 million in potential losses. So far this year, Ottimate has caught 6,026 payments with errors, accounting for $1.01 million in potential losses. Payment errors are expensive and hard to recover once funds leave the account. Halfway through the year, hotel accounts are already closing in on last year’s full total. Manual payment reviews miss what automated checks catch consistently, which is exactly why a final validation layer before disbursement matters, whether payment runs through ACH or virtual card. Productivity Benchmarks Invoice Lifecycle Time Benchmark : Hotel customers using Ottimate have reduced invoice lifecycle time from upload to approval from 11 days down to 5.3 days on average. In the first half of 2026, hotel customers hit 3.14 days, 36 percent faster than the benchmark. Hotel groups are continuing to accelerate even as invoice volume grows. For a property running month-end close on a tight calendar, that speed means fewer accruals to estimate and fewer surprises waiting in the aging report. AP Labor Savings Benchmark : Ottimate saves hotel groups $69,000 per account per year in labor by reducing invoice lifecycle time, the equivalent of freeing up one full employee’s time for higher-value work. In the first half of 2026, hotel accounts are saving 7.96 days per invoice compared to the manual baseline. Hotel accounts are compounding efficiency gains as both speed improves and volume grows. That’s the time a Property Accountant or AP Manager gets back from statement reconciliation and exception handling, and time a Controller gets back for the work that actually requires judgment. About This Report The Hotels AP Automation Benchmark Report: Summer 2026 Edition is published by Ottimate using aggregated, anonymized data from our hotel customer base. All benchmarks reflect real invoice processing data across independent properties, management companies, and multi-property hotel groups. This is the first edition; future editions will track trends and flag what’s driving the changes. body_text: Last updated July 26, 2026 Finding the right talent in 2026 requires more than posting jobs and waiting for applications. The best candidates are passive, already employed, and unlikely to stumble across your listing. AI people search tools solve this by surfacing candidate profiles, verified contact data, and automated outreach at scale. But not all people search tools are built for recruiting. This guide focuses specifically on AI people search platforms designed for hiring teams, not background check services built for tenant screening or personal investigations. What Is an AI People Search Tool for Recruiting? An AI people search tool for recruiting is a platform that uses machine learning and data intelligence to discover, rank, and contact candidates across multiple professional databases. Unlike background check services, which verify criminal history or financial records for compliance purposes, recruiting focused people search tools prioritize work history, skills, contact information, and candidate engagement. These platforms aggregate profiles from LinkedIn, GitHub, public records, job boards, and other sources, then use AI to match candidates to job requirements and automate outreach campaigns. Weekday exemplifies this distinction. It operates as a proactive hiring platform with a 300M+ database of verified professionals, multi-channel outreach automation, and AI-driven matching. The platform delivers 30 to 50% response rates on outbound campaigns because it focuses on finding mutual-fit candidates and reaching them through email, WhatsApp, and phone. This is fundamentally different from consumer-oriented people search tools like TruthFinder or Spokeo, which are prohibited from employment use under FCRA guidelines. Why AI People Search Tools for Recruiting Matter in 2026 Traditional job boards present a structural challenge for hiring teams because they reach a limited pool of active job seekers. Research shows most workers stay receptive to new opportunities while employed. These passive candidates rarely browse job boards, so direct outreach is the most effective way to reach them. Traditional inbound hiring misses this majority entirely. AI people search tools built for recruiting solve four specific problems: Limited Candidate Pool : Job boards surface only candidates who are actively searching. AI people search platforms index passive candidates who are employed, not job hunting, and often higher quality. Manual Sourcing Overhead : Recruiters spend 13+ hours per week on manual sourcing tasks like building Boolean queries, copying contact data, and drafting outreach emails. AI automates this entirely. Low Response Rates : Generic InMail messages on LinkedIn average 18 to 25% response rates . Multi-channel AI-driven outreach with personalized messaging consistently exceeds 30%. Data Fragmentation : Candidate information lives across LinkedIn, GitHub, Stack Overflow, company websites, and other sources. AI people search tools aggregate and enrich this data into unified profiles. Weekday addresses these pain points by combining a large verified talent database with automated outreach sequences across email, WhatsApp, and phone. The platform delivers interested, pre-vetted candidates to hiring teams without requiring recruiters to build searches manually or chase down contact information. What to Look for in an AI People Search Tool for Recruiters Not every AI people search platform is built for hiring. Background check services, personal investigation tools, and generic data brokers cannot legally be used for employment decisions. When evaluating recruiting focused AI people search tools, prioritize the following features: Multi-Source Database Coverage : The platform should aggregate profiles from professional networks, code repositories, and public records, not just LinkedIn. Look for 500M+ profiles minimum. Verified Contact Data : Email addresses and phone numbers should be verified and high-accuracy. Platforms with 90%+ deliverability rates save time and reduce bounce rates. AI-Powered Matching : Natural language search and semantic understanding beat Boolean strings. The AI should rank candidates by fit, not just keyword matches. Automated Outreach : Email sequences, follow-ups, and multi-channel campaigns should run on autopilot. The best platforms include WhatsApp and phone outreach in markets where those channels drive higher engagement. Compliance and Privacy : The platform must be built for employment use, not consumer background checks. FCRA-compliant tools are designed for hiring decisions; non-compliant tools are illegal to use for recruitment. Weekday checks every box. The platform provides access to 300M+ verified profiles, AI-drafted outreach with 50%+ response rates, and multi-channel campaigns that include WhatsApp and phone follow-ups. Because Weekday is purpose-built for hiring, it delivers candidates ready to interview, not just raw data that requires manual follow-up. How Recruiters and Hiring Teams Use AI People Search Tools Recruiters using AI people search tools in 2026 follow a proactive hiring workflow that prioritizes quality over volume: Strategy 1: Passive Candidate Discovery AI search filters surface candidates who match the role but are not actively applying Platforms like Weekday rank candidates by skills, tenure, company background, and likelihood to respond Strategy 2: Multi-Channel Outreach Automation AI-drafted email sequences personalized to each candidate's background WhatsApp and phone follow-ups in markets where those channels drive higher response rates Automated reminders and nurture campaigns keep candidates engaged Strategy 3: Talent Pool Building Save candidate searches and set up alerts for new profiles that match criteria Rediscover past applicants when new roles open Build pipelines for future hiring needs, not just active requisitions Strategy 4: Team Collaboration and Pipeline Management Share candidate lists across hiring managers and recruiters Track outreach status, response rates, and pipeline stages in one platform Integrate with ATS to move candidates seamlessly from sourcing to interview Strategy 5: Market Intelligence and Benchmarking Understand salary expectations and competitive landscape by role and location Identify companies with high concentrations of target talent Track hiring trends and talent availability in real time Strategy 6: Compliance and Reference Verification Platforms like Weekday include peer-vouching networks that deliver backchannel references within 24 hours Ensure outreach and data usage comply with employment regulations Avoid tools designed for consumer background checks, which violate FCRA when used for hiring Weekday differentiates itself by handling outreach end to end. Most sourcing platforms surface contact information and leave messaging, follow-up, and phone calls to the recruiter. Weekday runs those campaigns on the hiring team's behalf, including WhatsApp and phone outreach, which drives the response rate differential. For teams hiring engineering roles in India and the US, no other platform matches Weekday's database depth or outreach reach. Recruiters need AI people search tools because the best candidates are not actively applying to job boards. Research shows that 70% of the workforce is passive, meaning they are employed and not actively job hunting but would consider the right opportunity if approached directly. Job boards like Indeed and Naukri surface only the 30% who are actively looking, which often includes candidates between jobs or underperforming in their current roles. AI people search tools like Weekday solve this by indexing the full candidate pool, including passive candidates at top companies, and automating outreach to engage them. Weekday achieves 30 to 50% response rates on outbound campaigns, compared to sub-10% response rates on generic job board applications, because it reaches mutual-fit candidates directly rather than waiting for them to apply. What Is the Difference Between AI People Search Tools and Background Check Services? AI people search tools for recruiting are designed to discover candidates, surface work history and skills, and enable outreach for hiring purposes. They aggregate professional profiles from LinkedIn, GitHub, job boards, and other sources, then use AI to match candidates to roles and automate engagement. Background check services, in contrast, verify criminal history, credit records, and other personal information for compliance purposes. Crucially, consumer background check tools like TruthFinder, Spokeo, and BeenVerified cannot legally be used for employment decisions under FCRA (Fair Credit Reporting Act) guidelines. Recruiters must use platforms explicitly designed for hiring, such as Weekday, Gem, or HireEZ, which are compliant with employment regulations and focus on candidate discovery rather than background verification. What Are the Best AI People Search Tools for Recruiters in 2026? The best AI people search tools for recruiters in 2026 are Weekday, Juicebox (PeopleGPT), HireEZ, Gem, SeekOut, LinkedIn Recruiter, and Findem. Weekday leads the category for tech hiring in India and the US with 300M+ verified profiles, 50%+ response rates on multi-channel outreach, and automated campaigns across email, WhatsApp, and phone. Juicebox excels at natural language search across 800M+ profiles from 30+ sources. HireEZ offers strong multi-platform sourcing and diversity analytics. Gem provides an all-in-one ATS, CRM, and sourcing platform. SeekOut specializes in hard-to-fill roles with attribute-based search. LinkedIn Recruiter remains the default for LinkedIn-native sourcing. Findem delivers enterprise-grade talent intelligence with a 3D data model. The right choice depends on geography (Weekday for India, others for global), hiring volume, budget, and whether you need just sourcing or end-to-end candidate delivery. How Do AI People Search Tools Achieve Higher Response Rates Than LinkedIn InMail? AI people search tools achieve higher response rates than LinkedIn InMail (18 to 25% average) by combining better targeting, multi-channel outreach, and personalization at scale. Platforms like Weekday achieve 30 to 50% response rates because they surface only mutual-fit candidates who match the role requirements, then reach them through the channels that work: email, WhatsApp, and phone, not just InMail. The AI drafts personalized messages based on each candidate's background, skills, and career trajectory, which feels relevant rather than spammy. Automated follow-ups keep candidates engaged without manual effort. In markets like India where WhatsApp is the primary communication channel, adding WhatsApp and phone outreach dramatically increases response rates compared to email-only or InMail-only approaches. The result is fewer messages sent, higher response rates, and better candidate quality. Can Small Teams and Startups Afford AI People Search Tools? Yes, small teams and startups can afford AI people search tools in 2026 due to flexible pricing models and startup-friendly programs. Platforms like Juicebox start at $99/month with free trials. Gem offers its startup program with 6 months free plus 50% off the first paid year for companies with 1 to 30 employees. Weekday offers both Subscription (pay-as-you-go with outreach credits) and Contingency (success-fee based, no upfront cost) models that align with startup budgets and hiring cadence. Monthly billing options and usage-based pricing make these tools accessible to solo recruiters and small teams, whereas enterprise platforms like LinkedIn Recruiter Corporate ($9,000 to $15,000 per seat per year) and Findem ($6,000 to $100,000+ per year) are prohibitively expensive for early-stage companies. The key is matching the tool to your hiring volume and choosing platforms with transparent pricing and flexible contracts. Are AI People Search Tools Compliant for Employment Use? Yes, AI people search tools designed specifically for recruiting are compliant for employment use, but consumer background check services are not. Platforms like Weekday, Gem, HireEZ, and LinkedIn Recruiter are built for talent acquisition and comply with employment regulations including GDPR (Europe), CCPA (California), and applicable data privacy laws. They focus on professional information like work history, skills, and contact details, not sensitive personal data like criminal records or credit scores. In contrast, consumer people search tools like TruthFinder, Spokeo, and Intelius are subject to FCRA (Fair Credit Reporting Act) restrictions and cannot legally be used for hiring, tenant screening, or other employment decisions. Recruiters must ensure they use platforms explicitly designed for recruiting to avoid legal exposure. Always verify that the platform's terms of service allow employment use and that data sourcing and candidate outreach comply with local regulations.

How to Make Your Own Shift at Midnight-Style Skinwalker Game (No Code)
summary: Build your own skinwalker night shift horror game without coding. Here's how Six Midnight Shifts was made with Rosebud AI, step by step, in plain English.
body_text: Shift at Midnight was made by one person. That is worth sitting with for a second: the biggest co-op horror hit of the summer came from a solo developer, Bun Muen, working on a premise simple enough to explain in a sentence - you work a night shift, and some customers are not human. Simple premises are the ones worth building on. Six Midnight Shifts is a free skinwalker horror game inspired by Shift at Midnight, made with Rosebud AI without hand-writing code. Here is how to make your own version. Step 1: Describe the fantasy, not the feature list Rosebud turns a plain-English description into a working game. Lead with the feeling. Something like: 'A first-person night shift in a rural convenience store. Customers come to the counter one at a time. Some of them are not human. I can check their ID against a records computer, and I have a gun under the register.' You will get something playable in minutes. That first version is a starting point, not the game - the iteration is where it becomes good. Step 2: Build the verification loop first The heart of this genre is one decision made under pressure: serve, refuse, or shoot. Get that working before anything else. Ask for a records computer the player can look things up in, an ID the customer hands over, and a mismatch system - a face that does not match the photo, a birth date that contradicts the record, an answer that is one word wrong. Test it obsessively. If the tells are too obvious the game is boring; if they are invisible it is unfair. That balance is the whole design. Step 3: Make the mundane work stressful What makes Shift at Midnight work is that verifying identities is not your only job. Add the boring tasks - restocking, cleaning, running the register - and put impatient customers on a timer. Now the player has to split attention, and that is when they miss the detail that kills them. Step 4: Escalate across nights Structure the game as a run of shifts rather than one endless session. Night one teaches the rules. By night four the anomalies are subtler, the queue is longer, and the thing at the counter has stopped bothering to hide. Six shifts is a good length - long enough to build dread, short enough to finish. Step 5: Punish the wrong kind of certainty Make shooting a real customer a genuine failure, not a slap on the wrist. A gun that solves everything removes the tension you spent four steps building. The fear should be of being wrong in either direction. Step 6: Publish and share Publishing from Rosebud gives your game its own page anyone can play in a browser, desktop or mobile, with no download and no store approval. That is how Six Midnight Shifts shipped. Shortcut: remix instead of starting over You do not have to begin from a blank prompt. Open Six Midnight Shifts on Rosebud and remix it - you get the full working game as your starting point, then change the setting or the monster. A hospital night shift, a border checkpoint, a lighthouse, a space station airlock: same loop, new nightmare. Frequently asked questions Do I need to know how to code? No. You describe what you want in plain English and Rosebud AI writes the code. You can open and edit the code if you want to, but it is not required. Is Rosebud AI free to try? Yes, you can start building for free at rosebud.ai . How long does a game like this take to make? A rough playable version takes minutes. Getting the tells and the difficulty curve to feel right is the part that takes real iteration. Can I remix someone else's game? Yes. Public Rosebud games can be remixed, which hands you a full working copy to modify as your own project. title: The Next Contact Center Security Threat May Sound Completely Human
summary: AI-generated voices are making voice phishing more realistic and scalable. Learn why contact centers need stronger conversation monitoring, real-time agent guidance, automated QA, and human oversight to prepare for the next generation of security threats.
body_text: Contact center agents have always been trained to recognize suspicious behavior. An unusual request, inconsistent information, or a caller who seems to be following a script can all raise red flags. But what happens when the person on the other end of the phone sounds completely natural? Recent advances in voice AI are making that question increasingly important. Today's systems can carry on fluid conversations with realistic voices, natural pacing, and increasingly convincing emotional expression. The same technology creating exciting new customer experiences can also be used by bad actors. New research suggests the threat isn't theoretical. AI Is Changing the Economics of Voice Phishing A July 2026 study examined whether current AI models could be used to automate voice phishing, or "vishing," attacks. Researchers tested several leading voice models in a large-scale experiment involving 4,100 U.S. adults and found that some AI voices were rated as comparably persuasive to human voices, with some even slightly outperforming the human baseline. Across the five scam categories researchers tested, 16.5% of participants indicated that they would or might comply with the request. In "relative in distress" scenarios, that figure reached as high as 36%. But perhaps the most important finding wasn't about persuasion at all. It was about economics. Traditional voice phishing requires people to make calls, which limits how many victims an attacker can realistically target. The researchers concluded that human-operated vishing is generally uneconomical at U.S. wage levels, while AI-powered vishing appears economically viable using several of the models they tested. AI doesn't necessarily have to become better at deception than humans. It just has to make deception cheap enough to scale. You May Not Be Able to Hear the Difference There's another reason this matters for contact centers: simply listening for a "robotic" voice may no longer be an effective defense. Separate 2026 research asked people to distinguish AI-generated voices from human-recorded voices in simulated vishing scenarios. Participants performed poorly, with an average accuracy of just 37.5%. Three-quarters of the AI-generated clips were classified as human by the majority of participants. The characteristics people traditionally associate with authenticity, such as pauses, vocal variation, cadence, and emotion, can increasingly be reproduced by synthetic voices. That changes the security equation. If an agent can't reliably determine whether a caller is human based on how they sound, organizations need other signals to determine whether the conversation itself is suspicious. Contact Centers Are an Attractive Target Contact centers sit at an unusual intersection of customer service and security. Agents are specifically trained to be helpful. They routinely help customers reset credentials, access accounts, update personal information, investigate transactions, and resolve unusual situations. In healthcare, financial services, insurance, travel, and other industries, they may also have access to extremely sensitive information. Those responsibilities make the contact center a natural target for social engineering. The risk becomes even greater if AI allows attackers to conduct thousands of convincing conversations at a fraction of the previous cost. An attacker doesn't need every call to succeed. At sufficient scale, even a relatively small success rate can become meaningful. And because the caller may sound perfectly normal, putting the burden entirely on the individual agent becomes increasingly unrealistic. The Conversation Itself Becomes a Security Signal This is where conversation intelligence can play a much larger role. Instead of asking an agent to independently recognize every potential threat, organizations can analyze conversations for patterns that might warrant additional attention. That could include unusual requests, repeated attempts to bypass standard procedures, unexpected combinations of account activity, or sudden increases in certain types of interactions. Research published this summer in Scientific Reports explored a similar idea at the network level, using call-log patterns and machine learning to proactively identify voice-phishing networks rather than waiting until individual victims reported fraud. For contact centers, the broader principle is important: security can't depend exclusively on whether one employee thinks a caller sounds suspicious. The organization needs visibility across conversations. Real-Time Guidance Can Become a Security Layer Conversation monitoring becomes even more valuable when insights can reach the agent while the interaction is still happening. Imagine an agent receives a seemingly ordinary call involving an unusual account request. As the conversation develops, real-time agent assist recognizes that certain behaviors require additional verification and reminds the agent of the appropriate procedure. The agent doesn't need to diagnose whether they're speaking with a sophisticated AI system. They simply need to follow the right process. This is where capabilities like accurate transcription, real-time agent assist, automated QA, and compliance monitoring can work together. MosaicVoice can help organizations identify important moments in conversations, provide timely guidance to agents, and evaluate interactions at scale rather than relying solely on manual call reviews. The objective isn't to label every unusual conversation as fraud. It's to give organizations and their agents more visibility when something deserves a closer look. Human Oversight Becomes More Important, Not Less There's an interesting irony in all of this. As AI becomes more sophisticated, human oversight may become more important. Organizations will need people to investigate emerging patterns, refine verification processes, coach agents on new threats, and continuously update the guidance provided during conversations. Automated QA can help identify whether those processes are actually being followed across thousands of interactions rather than a small sample of calls. The strongest defense will likely combine AI's ability to recognize patterns at scale with human judgment about what those patterns mean. That's especially important because the threat itself will continue changing. The Bottom Line For years, voice phishing had a natural constraint: people. Attackers needed someone to make the calls, carry the conversation, respond naturally, and persuade the person on the other end. Voice AI is beginning to remove that constraint. The next generation of fraudulent calls may not sound robotic, awkward, or obviously suspicious. They may sound completely normal. That means contact centers need to look beyond the sound of the caller and start paying closer attention to the behavior happening within and across conversations. In the age of AI-generated voices, the question may no longer be, "Does this caller sound real?" It may be, "Does this conversation look right?"

title: How to Build a Lead Operations System From Scratch
summary: Most companies don't build a lead operations system. They accumulate one. A form tool here, a Zapier connection there, a routing rule someone set up 18 months
body_text: Most companies don't build a lead operations system. They accumulate one. A form tool here, a Zapier connection there, a routing rule someone set up 18 months ago that nobody fully understands. By the time you have 10+ lead sources and 8+ reps, the duct tape is holding together a system that nobody designed intentionally. If you're starting from scratch — or if your current setup has gotten painful enough that you need to rebuild — here's the architecture that actually works. What a lead operations system actually does Lead ops covers four jobs. Most teams have tools for one or two of them and gaps in the rest. Job What it does What most teams use Where it breaks Capture Collects lead data from every source — forms, ads, third-party providers, events HubSpot Forms, Typeform, native CMS forms Different tools per source. Inconsistent fields. No qualification at capture. Qualification Determines if the lead is worth pursuing and how urgently Manual SDR review or basic lead scoring Happens too late (on the call instead of at the form), or uses vanity signals instead of real intent Routing Matches the lead to the right rep based on relevant attributes CRM round-robin or manual assignment Doesn't account for territory, deal size, product interest, or rep availability Response Contacts the lead with the right message at the right speed Rep gets a CRM notification and acts when they see it Slow, generic, and disconnected from routing and qualification data A real lead ops system connects all four. The lead is captured, qualified, routed, and responded to in one continuous flow — not four disconnected steps with handoff gaps between them. Step 1: Map every lead source into one capture layer Before you build anything, list every way a lead enters your system. Website forms, paid ad landing pages, third-party lead providers (G2, Capterra, etc.), event registrations, chatbot conversations, partner referrals. Most teams have 5–15 distinct sources. Every source should flow through the same capture layer with the same core fields. That doesn't mean every form looks identical — a demo request form and a whitepaper download form ask different questions. But the data schema should be consistent: every lead, regardless of source, should arrive in your system with the same base fields (name, email, company) plus qualifying data where applicable. If different sources use different tools with different field names, you'll spend forever normalizing data downstream. Standardize at the point of capture. Step 2: Qualify at capture, not after The most expensive place to qualify a lead is on a phone call with an SDR. The cheapest place is on the form itself. Add 2–4 qualifying questions to your high-intent forms (demo requests, contact forms, pricing inquiries): company size, budget range, timeline, and use case. Use conditional logic — if they select "just researching," route to nurture. If they select "evaluating now, budget approved," route to a senior AE immediately. Low-intent captures (blog subscriptions, content downloads) don't need full qualification. But they should still capture enough data to segment — at minimum, company size and role. [IMAGE: A simple flowchart showing a form submission branching into three paths based on qualification answers: "High intent → Senior AE (instant)," "Medium intent → SDR (same day)," "Low intent → Nurture sequence (automated)." Clean, minimal, white background, blue ( #4F6DF5 ) accent, flat design.] Step 3: Build routing rules that match your actual sales structure Your routing logic should reflect how your sales team actually works, not how your CRM's default assignment feature works. Start by defining the variables that determine which rep should get which lead: territory/geography, deal size tier, product or service line, industry vertical, rep availability and current capacity. Most teams need 2–3 of these. Complex sales orgs need all five. Then build rules in priority order. Territory first, then deal size, then product interest, with availability as a tiebreaker. If no rule matches, the lead goes to a default queue with an SLA — not into a black hole. Test your routing by running your last 100 leads through the new logic on paper before you deploy. If more than 5% would end up in the wrong place, refine the rules. Step 4: Automate the first response The first message a lead receives should happen within 60 seconds of form submission and should include three things: acknowledgment of what they asked about, the name of the person who will help them, and a clear next step (scheduling link or expectation of when they'll hear back). This message should be automated — triggered by the routing decision, not by a human noticing a notification. The rep follows up after the automated response, but the lead never sits in silence wondering if anyone received their request. Step 5: Connect measurement end-to-end The final piece is visibility. You need to track four metrics continuously: speed-to-lead (form submit to first outreach), routing accuracy (percentage of leads that go to the correct rep without reassignment), lead-to-meeting rate (percentage of captured leads that result in a booked meeting), and cost per meeting booked (total spend divided by meetings, not leads). If you can see these four numbers in real time, you can diagnose and fix problems before they compound. If you can't, you're flying blind. Where Surface fits Surface was built to be the lead ops system — capture, qualification, routing, and response in one connected layer. If you're building from scratch or rebuilding from duct tape, Surface handles the architecture described in this post out of the box. If your current system requires 4+ tools and a Zapier flowchart to move a lead from form to rep, you don't have a system. You have a workaround. Surface was built to replace it.

title: Announcing Ubicloud Machine Images
summary: Today, we are excited to introduce Ubicloud Machine Images (UMIs)! UMIs let you capture the disk of a configured VM and use it to create new VMs.
body_text: Announcing Ubicloud Machine Images August 12, 2026 · 2 min read Hadi Moshayedi Principal Software Engineer Today, we are excited to introduce Ubicloud Machine Images (UMIs) ! UMIs let you capture the disk of a configured VM and use it to create new VMs. Many workloads need more than a clean operating system. Before a VM is useful, you may need to install packages, deploy an application, and configure monitoring. Repeating those steps for every new VM slows down launches and can produce differences between machines. With machine images, you perform that setup once. Configure a VM, stop it, and capture its disk as an immutable image version. Future VMs can then start from the captured state. Capture once, launch repeatedly Machine images are useful whenever you need to launch multiple VMs with the same preconfigured environment. You might use one to package an application server with its dependencies, create standardized development or CI environments, launch prebuilt sandboxes for AI agents and other ephemeral workloads, or keep a known-good system image for quickly recreating a workload. Instead of repeating setup on every VM, you can prepare and test the environment once, then launch new VMs directly from that image. A managed database service is a good example of this pattern. Ubicloud operates a managed database service where each database runs on an isolated VM. Every VM needs the same database packages, backup tooling, monitoring, and platform configuration before it can serve a customer. This common environment is effectively a versioned release artifact. Instead of rebuilding it whenever a customer creates a database, the company prepares and validates it once, then captures it as a machine image version, like db-service@v1. When a customer creates a database, the control plane launches a VM from this image. Most of the preparation is already complete. First boot only needs to apply instance-specific configuration, such as credentials and backup settings, start the services and run health checks. Every new database therefore starts from the same tested foundation without repeating the complete image-building process. When Ubicloud updates the operating system, database packages, backup tooling, or monitoring agents, we prepare and validate a new image version: db-service@v2. Once v2 finishes capturing, it becomes the image's latest version, so new VMs created from db-service@latest pick it up automatically. v1 remains unchanged and can still be requested by label to reproduce earlier deployments. If any issues arise with db-service@v2 , we can point db-service@latest back to db-service@v1. New VMs created from db-service@latest then use v1 again. Nothing has to be built or captured again. Available today Machine images are available today and you can start using them. You can create and manage them through the Ubicloud console, the CLI ( ubi mi ), or the API. A few things to keep in mind when capturing a version: the source VM must be stopped and have a single disk of at most 40 GiB, and a VM created from the image needs a boot disk at least as large as the captured disk. Because the new VM inherits everything on the source disk, generalize the source VM before capturing it. Machine images are billed according to the physical storage used by their archives. We omit unused disk regions and compress the remaining data, so the stored size can be significantly smaller than the source VM's disk. Machine images currently cost $0.15 per GiB per month . See the machine images documentation to get started.

title: Designing with Empathy: How Senior designer is Transforming the Student Loan Experience at SoFi
summary: We sat down with Julie Palmer, Senior Designer on our Borrow team who has dedicated nearly four years to optimizing SoFi’s student loan products.
body_text: When you think about the student loan process, it can be extremely daunting. For many applicants, seeking a private loan or navigating a refinance happens at the end of a long, emotional rollercoaster of financial decision-making. But at SoFi, changing that narrative is a design priority. We sat down with Julie Palmer, Senior Designer on our Borrow team who has dedicated nearly four years to optimizing SoFi’s student loan products. Julie shared her journey from SoFi intern to full-time design advocate, how she uses deep user research to solve complex member problems, and what it really means to design with empathy. From Intern to Expert: Julie’s SoFi Journey Julie’s history with SoFi began in 2022. She joined the team as an intern, working on broad, cross-functional projects across the lending space. After completing her master’s degree, she knew she wanted to return full-time. “As a new grad, the student loan space was something I had just lived through myself," Julie explains. "Understanding your audience is critical for a designer. Having gone through the mindset of obtaining loans, managing them, and working to pay them off gave me an innate empathy for our members. I knew exactly what they were feeling." Now approaching her fourth year as a full-time designer on the Borrow team, Julie works exclusively across both of SoFi's student loan products: Private Student Loans and Student Loan Refinancing. Over the years, her deep understanding of the user journey has made her a go-to champion for the student experience. Navigating the Peak: Designing for the Financial Gap Designing for private student loans comes with unique psychological and logistical challenges. Unlike standard retail or banking products, private student loans are highly seasonal. "If you look at our annual traffic, it’s a wave that peaks in the summer," Julie notes. "That’s when students and families are scrambling to secure funding for the upcoming school year." Understanding when members interact with the product is only half the battle; designers must also understand why. "By the time someone applies for a private student loan, it’s often their last resort," Julie says. "They’ve exhausted federal loans, scholarships, grants, and family contributions. They’ve had tough kitchen-table conversations about budgets, fought with parents about school choices, and filled out the FAFSA. They come to us at the end of a very draining cycle. Our design language has to acknowledge that baggage and meet them exactly where they are." Impact in Action: Bridging Member Needs and Business Goals For Julie, successful product design at SoFi isn't just about making an interface look sleek, it’s about finding the symbiosis between member problems and business objectives. She highlighted a few recent projects where user-centric design completely shifted the product experience: 1. The Student Loan Refinance Comparison Tool When members look to refinance, they often bring a messy portfolio of multiple loans, each with different interest rates, terms, and monthly balances. Previously, SoFi would present refinance offers, but members lacked an easy way to see how those offers stacked up against their current financial reality. Julie helped design a true apples-to-apples comparison tool. Directly beneath each SoFi offer, the system dynamically calculates and displays the exact difference. "Refinancing is a massive decision, especially if you’re weighing the loss of federal benefits," Julie says. "Building a transparent, borrower-centric tool helped members confidently decide if refinancing was right for their budget and goals." 2. Solving for the Graduate Student Federal Gap Following major federal loan policy changes that eliminated certain funding paths, Julie and her team quickly pivoted to design specialized graduate products. New Graduate Programs: With an influx of graduate borrowers this year, the team set out to build products that address their needs. Julie worked on an experience that qualifies certain graduate degrees for benefits that speak to their needs, like extended grace periods and deferments for medical, dental, and law students. Advance Approval: Instead of forcing grad students to endure a stressful, hard-credit-check prequalification process every single school year, Julie helped design Advance Approval . Borrowers are prequalified for their entire degree amount upfront, giving them peace of mind while allowing them to simply request the necessary funds year by year. How do you ensure the member’s voice actually drives the product roadmap? We work hand-in-hand with our research team. For example, because of the seasonal nature of private student loans, we run a survey every summer to capture sentiment while students are in the process of taking out loans. We now have over five years of year-over-year insights mapping how the student landscape, anxieties, and digital behaviors are evolving. When we introduce a new feature, we run user research to build products that truly solve user problems, and we continuously check in to make sure our experiences are working for everyone. How do you handle situations where business goals seem to conflict with user experience goals? That’s where the real design work happens. When the Advanced Approval project first came to my desk, the business goal was serialization—ensuring students come back to SoFi for year two, three, and four. Instead of designing a rigid retention loop, I stepped back and asked: What is the ideal experience that would make a student WANT to come back? The answer was minimizing friction and anxiety. By designing a system that prequalifies them for their whole degree upfront and removes repetitive hard credit checks in years two and three, we simultaneously solved the user’s anxiety and achieved the business’s serialization goal. True alignment comes from advocating for the user's peace of mind. What advice do you have for designers looking to join the team at SoFi? Be ready to look at the big picture. Lending and financial tech are incredibly complex backend systems, but our job is to distill that complexity into absolute clarity for someone who might be having a stressful day. If you love deep user research, cross-functional collaboration, and turning high-stakes financial journeys into empowering, transparent experiences, this is the place to do it.
